pr_body:
This PR implements MSAA for the 2D/Canvas renderer. (Implements godotengine/godot-proposals#1297) In addition, this might improve the situation for godotengine/godot-proposals#1126.

Detailed changes:
- Implement 2D MSAA support for the Canvas renderer, which can be controlled separately from 3D MSAA for maximum flexibility (2X, 4X and 8X are supported, same as for 3D)
	- implementation should be efficient since we can use automatic resolving without the need of VkCmdResolveImage, which has a negative impact on bandwidth
	- can be set for each viewport separately
	- currently not implemented for OpenGL implementation (but should be easy once the OpenGL renderer is done)
- Rename project settings, viewport properties and methods from msaa to msaa_2/3d for clarity
- Minor code restructuring and comment style fixes

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Selecting 8× MSAA on Apple M1 GPU crashes the editor
issue_context.body:
*Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/53940.*

### Godot version

4.0.dev (489f11ee0)

### System information

Apple Mac mini 2020 (M1), macOS Monterey 12.1

### Issue description

The M1 GPU only supports 4× MSAA at most, yet Godot's Vulkan renderer allows setting it to 8× even on GPUs that don't support it. Instead, the MSAA value should be clamped to the highest value supported by the hardware.
Additionally, the MSAA property hint in the project settings could be automatically modified to denote that specific values are unsupported on the user's machine.

I haven't checked whether this occurs in `3.x`'s GLES3 and GLES2 renderers yet.
**Edit:** I've tested a few games such as [Yamagi Quake 2](https://yamagi.org/quake2/) and noticed that MSAA is clamped to 4× when trying to use 8× MSAA there.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new project. Add a MeshInstance3D node with a BoxMesh resource.
- Open the Project Settings and enable the **Advanced** toggle.
- Set MSAA to 8×.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
> I haven't checked whether this occurs in `3.x`'s GLES3 and GLES2 renderers yet.

My M1 does not crash using MSAA 8x/16x on either GLES2 and GLES3, so this only applies to Vulkan.

- System info: M1 MacBook Air 2020, also running MacOS Monterey 12.1
- Godot version: `v3.4.stable.official`

review_comments: You're right, we could, but I wasn't done for all the other render_target_set_xxx methods so I'd rather do it in a refactoring PR later.
This one needs the early return because it calls a function. The others don't call functions so they don't need early returns.

Bringing this back. Since this function will call ``update_render_target`` it needs an early out if the desired msaa is the same as current. We don't want to reallocate resources if the value doesn't change

We should likely have an error or warning if the user sets the 2D MSAA differently than the 3D MSAA as they share a framebuffer. 

Once we add Post effects that require a separate pass, we could remove the requirement for the MSAA to be the same and then properly resolve and copy the 3D color texture to the 2D Framebuffer. For now implementing that will be overkill.

Since 3D MSAA is not yet functional, 3D breaks as soon as you enable 2D MSAA. This could be fixed, but I think it would be better to implement it later (properly) when post effects have been added. Right now it just feels a bit messy, so I think it's better to just remove the GLES3 implementation for now.
is there any reason to set Msaa2D from settings but not Msaa3D? does this mean someone working on 3D needs to hit the Play button to actually see the final quality of the game?

MSAA for 3D is set in `node_3d_editor_plugin`, so it also works in the editor. Unfortunately, in the `canvas_item_editor_plugin `there is currently no callback like `_project_settings_changed`, so I had to place it in `editor_node`
The 3D MSAA level is already set on project setting changes in `node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp`.
for consistency, purposes, what is the best value to use in the previews? always use MSAA_4X or use whatever is default on ProjectSettings?

I think editor previews should always use 4× MSAA, which is a good compromise between performance and quality. 8× MSAA barely has any visual impact, but it has a huge performance impact in modern rendering engines. Some GPUs (such as Apple M1) don't support 8× MSAA either.
